diagonals.title: diagonals
diagonals.explanation: The diagonal lines separate tens from units and collect values with the same place value.
diagonals.guidance: Draw each diagonal from the top right to the bottom left of its cell. Add along the diagonal bands.
examples: For a cell product of 24, write 2 above the diagonal and 4 below it.
For 23 × 14, the cells contain 02, 03, 08 and 12. Starting at the bottom right, the diagonal totals are 2; then 1 + 8 + 3 = 12 (write 2, carry 1); then 0 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 3. Read 322.

tens-and-units.title: Tens
tens-and-units.explanation: A two-digit product has a tens digit and a units digit.
tens-and-units.guidance: Write both digits in each cell, including a zero tens digit for a product below 10.
examples: 3 × 2 = 6: write 0 above the diagonal and 6 below.
7 × 8 = 56: put 5 in the upper-left tens triangle and 6 in the lower-right units triangle. For 2 × 4 = 8, write 08: the 0 still belongs in the tens triangle.

carry.title: carry
carry.explanation: Ten units of one place value make one unit of the next place value.
carry.guidance: Write the units digit of a diagonal total; carry the tens to the next diagonal.
examples: A diagonal total of 17 means write 7 and carry 1.
If a diagonal contains 7, 6 and 4, its total is 17. Write 7 at that diagonal’s end and add a carried 1 to the next diagonal to the left. If that diagonal originally totals 8, it now totals 9.

leading-zeros.title: leading zeros
leading-zeros.explanation: Zeros before the first non-zero digit of a whole number do not change its value.
leading-zeros.guidance: Leave out leading zeros when reading the answer, but keep zeros between other digits.
examples: 12 × 34 gives the outside digits 0, 4, 0, 8. Read 408. The first zero can go, but the middle zero means there are no tens and must stay.
